title: I KNOW WHAT I WANT TO SELL. NOW WHAT?
content:
You came here to answer one question: what should I sell?

If you can now describe a specific product, service, subscription, consumable, or selling relationship that fits you well enough to investigate seriously, this library has done its job.

You do not need every detail solved. You need a direction specific enough that the next questions are about building and selling THAT business rather than continuing to search the entire internet for business ideas.

WRITE YOUR BUSINESS DIRECTION STATEMENT
Use this structure as a starting point:

I want to sell [SPECIFIC THING] to [SPECIFIC CUSTOMER], using [OWNERSHIP / SELLING STRUCTURE] because [WHY THIS DIRECTION FITS ME OR THE CUSTOMER].

Examples:

I want to sell a one-off digital guide I create for first-time dog owners who need a simple preparation checklist.

I want to launch my own branded protein powder through a contract manufacturer for women who struggle to consume enough protein through meals.

I want to provide recurring remote bookkeeping for small home-service businesses that need reliable accounts payable and receivable support.

I want to recommend editing software to beginner photographers through an affiliate relationship, after verifying the current program terms.

YOUR STATEMENT IS A DIRECTION, NOT A GUARANTEE
You may still need to verify demand, costs, suppliers, program terms, regulations, licenses, competition, technical feasibility, or other facts. That research can change the direction. That is normal.

The important change is that your research now has a target.

FINAL CHECK
Before moving on, can you answer:
What am I selling?
Who is it for?
Do I own the product/offer, resell it, refer it, or provide the service?
What important assumptions still need verification?
Why does this direction fit my current priorities and constraints?

If one of those answers is still missing, return to the relevant guide instead of forcing a conclusion.

YOU HAVE SOMETHING TO SELL. NEXT: HOW WILL YOU SELL IT?
That is a different problem.

Choosing what to sell does not automatically tell you how customers will discover it, how you will communicate the value, where the transaction happens, or what sales system fits you.

Those questions belong to the next stage.

OPTIONAL NEXT STEP: WANT HANDS-ON HELP FROM HERE?

If you want more than a self-guided process, I also have a hands-on coaching path for some people whose direction fits the businesses and systems my team can actually help with.

The coaching itself is free, but it starts with interviews because this is a working relationship, not an unlimited free consulting offer. We are looking for mutual fit.

There is a practical reason we can offer coaching without charging a coaching fee: in the business structures where we work together, your success can contribute to ours too. That aligns our incentives. I want to be transparent about that rather than pretending the coaching has no business purpose for us.

I am an Amway Independent Business Owner, and the experienced coaches I work with teach an established network-marketing path. I am also experimenting with a newer model that combines that foundation with digital information products, subscriptions, affiliate relationships, and licensed products.

Depending on the direction you chose, working with me may involve network marketing, my digital products, affiliate or licensed-product opportunities, or another path that actually fits what you selected. You do not need to choose my business. The whole point was to help you choose yours.

If an opportunity involves purchases, qualification requirements, fees, licenses, or other financial commitments, those should be explained before you decide whether to participate.

YOUR NEXT MOVE
Save your Business Direction Statement somewhere you can find it. Use it as the starting point for the research and decisions that follow.

You no longer need to answer "What could I sell?"

You need to find out whether THIS is the thing you want to build.
